**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551**
**Member:** Cameron Brooks
**Member ID:** W295648415
**Reference number:** POC-0948834B99-90261
**Date of denial notice:** August 25, 2026
**Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery* (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/4827/pdf-Spine-Surgery-2024-10-20.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Anthem's denial of the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery. The notice dated August 25, 2026 states that the records do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before surgery. I am asking Anthem to reconsider that decision, because my records document exactly the conservative care the plan's own guideline describes, and my surgeon has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am appealing within the timeframe stated in my notice, which says my appeal must be received by February 21, 2027.

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

**1. What conservative management must include.**

The guideline states:

> "Conservative management1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records show each of these:

- **Physical therapy:** supervised physical therapy including cervical traction and postural training, 8 weeks, from May 3, 2026 to June 28, 2026, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Complementary strategies (more than one):** NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on May 5, 2026 that gave two weeks of partial relief.

That is physical therapy plus two additional conservative treatments, not one.

**2. Completion of a full course, and the result.**

The guideline also states:

> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care"

and

> "Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation"

I completed the full 18-visit course of physical therapy through discharge. My symptoms are documented as 14 months of progressive neck pain, unrelieved by rest, with radicular pain and numbness into my right thumb and index finger and weakness. The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief and the injection gave only two weeks of partial relief. The records describe progression, not improvement.

**3. The six-week duration the guideline itself states.**

The guideline states:

> "Unremitting radicular pain which has not responded to at least 6 weeks of appropriate conservative management (physical therapy optional)"

My supervised physical therapy alone ran eight weeks, from May 3 to June 28, 2026, on top of four months of NSAIDs and an injection. This is the only duration threshold quoted in the excerpts available to me, and my care exceeds it.

**4. Imaging that correlates with my symptoms and exam.**

The guideline states:

> "All imaging must be performed and read by an independent radiologist. If discrepancies should arise in the interpretation of the imaging, the radiologist report will supersede. The results of all imaging studies should correlate with the clinical findings in support of the requested procedure."

and introduces a set of criteria with this line:

> "When imaging studies demonstrate nerve root compression due to herniated disc or spondylotic osteophyte correlating with the distribution of signs and symptoms, and ANY of the following criteria apply:"

My MRI of the cervical spine dated June 29, 2026 shows a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. My symptoms are on the right, in the thumb and index finger, and my exam shows positive provocative testing on the affected side with a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. The imaging and the clinical findings match.

Within that list, the guideline includes:

> "Objective neurologic findings which correlate with a cervical nerve root impingement"

My documented exam findings — positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, with numbness in the right thumb and index finger and weakness — are objective findings that correlate with the C6 nerve root compression seen on MRI.

**5. The guideline's own waiver provision.**

The guideline states:

> "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when myelopathy, weakness, or bladder disturbance is present."

Weakness is documented in my records, alongside the documented neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. I do not need to rely on this provision, because I completed conservative care — but under the plan's own language, a conservative-care trial is not the deciding issue where weakness is present.

**6. Tobacco status.**

The guideline states:

> "Tobacco cessation. Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to spinal surgery is strongly recommended to reduce the risk of pseudoarthrosis."

My records state that I am a non-smoker. My records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, and a BMI of 29.

## Two requests for clarity

First, the guideline defines a pain and function threshold:

> "significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs"

My records as I have them document 14 months of progressive pain unrelieved by rest, radicular pain, numbness and weakness, but I do not want to state a number or a list of activities that my chart does not state. If this definition is part of the basis for the denial, I ask Anthem to say so, and I will ask my surgeon's office to supply [pain rating as documented in the chart] and [specific ADLs/IADLs affected, as documented].

Second, two of the provisions above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I do not have in front of me. The denial notice does not identify which specific criterion within the guideline Anthem found unmet. I ask that the plan identify, in writing, the exact criteria it applied and where my records were found to fall short, so that I can respond to the actual basis for the decision. Other than the excerpts I have quoted above, I am not quoting plan language, and I am not attributing any requirement to Anthem that I have not quoted.

## What I am asking for

I ask Anthem to overturn the denial and approve CPT 22551 as requested by Dr. Marchetti. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask for a written explanation identifying the specific guideline criterion relied upon, the credentials and specialty of the reviewer, and instructions for the next level of review, including external review.

I am enclosing, or asking my surgeon's office to send:

- The physical therapy discharge note covering May 3 – June 28, 2026 (18 visits)
- The MRI cervical spine report dated June 29, 2026
- Office notes from Dr. Marchetti documenting my exam findings and medical necessity
- Records of NSAID use and the corticosteroid injection dated May 5, 2026
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office identifies]

Thank you for reviewing this appeal and my complete records.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
**Cameron Brooks**
Member ID: W295648415
Reference number: POC-0948834B99-90261
